personas.name: Administrator
personas.goal: Manage users, roles, tenants, features, content types, deployment plans, security settings, and the full system configuration.

personas.name: Editor
personas.goal: Edit and publish content items across the CMS.

personas.name: Moderator
personas.goal: Moderate user-generated content and manage community contributions.

personas.name: Author
personas.goal: Create and edit content items for publication.

personas.name: Contributor
personas.goal: Create content drafts that can be reviewed and published by others.

personas.name: Registered User / Site Visitor
personas.goal: Register, log in, manage personal profile, and view published content.

personas.name: Integration Developer
personas.goal: Consume the REST, GraphQL, and MetaWeblog/XML-RPC APIs to build integrations and headless applications.

epics.name: Azure Blob / Data Lake Media Integration

definition_of_ready: No open question or unresolved ambiguity on the story.
Every epic this epic depends on is marked Done.
Every screen, endpoint, and entity the story names exists in the model.
Acceptance criteria written as Gherkin scenarios.
Story is estimated and fits within one sprint.
definition_of_done: Every Gherkin scenario passes as an automated test: unit/API-contract tests via xUnit on Ubuntu and Windows; end-to-end flows via Playwright on Chromium.
Every endpoint the story builds passes its contract test against openapi.json.
NFRs applicable to this story (performance, security, accessibility) are demonstrably met.

The change is reviewed (pull request approved), merged through the GitHub Actions pipeline (build release config, warnings-as-errors, analyzers, unit tests on Ubuntu and Windows, browser tests), and deployed to the Staging environment on Azure App Service.

features.name: User Management & Identity
features.description: User registration, login, authentication, password management, and self-service profile editing.

features.name: Roles & Access Control
features.description: Role creation, editing, cloning, deletion, permission assignment, and authorization enforcement.

features.name: Content Management
features.description: Content item creation, editing, publishing, unpublishing, drafting, cloning, removing, restoring, and display.

features.name: Content Type Management
features.description: Content type and content part field definition: creating, editing, and managing content type structure.

features.name: Module & Feature Extensibility
features.description: Enabling, disabling, and managing modules and features; dependency-aware enable/disable.

features.name: Site Setup & Tenant Provisioning
features.description: Initial site setup, multi-tenant administration, tenant creation, and AutoSetup provisioning.

features.name: Deployment Plans
features.description: Creating, exporting, importing, and executing deployment plans with typed deployment steps.

features.name: Query Management
features.description: Creating, editing, running, and deleting named queries (Lucene, SQL, GraphQL).

features.name: Background Processing
features.description: Modular background service with per-tenant task execution, distributed locking, and configurable polling intervals.

features.name: Workflow Automation
features.description: Content-event-driven workflows with task activities (CreateContentTask, PublishContentTask, UpdateContentTask, etc.) and user-task gating.

features.name: Media Storage
features.description: Media management with Azure Blob, Azure Data Lake, and Amazon S3 storage backends; media picker in content editor.

features.name: API & Integration
features.description: REST content API, GraphQL API, named query API, MetaWeblog/XML-RPC remote publishing, and remote deployment.

features.name: Search Indexing
features.description: Elasticsearch and Lucene search indexing with index management and query execution.

features.name: SMS & Email Notifications
features.description: Email provider (Azure Communication Services) for verification emails and SMS provider configuration.

features.name: Data Persistence & Migrations
features.description: YesSql-backed schema management, DataMigrationManager, and per-feature versioned migrations.

roles.name: Administrator
roles.description: Full administrative access; system role and admin role; manages users, roles, tenants, features, content types, deployment plans, recipes, templates, workflows, security settings.

roles.name: Contributor
roles.description: Can create but not publish content.

roles.name: Anonymous
roles.description: Special system role — unauthenticated visitors. IsAuthenticated = false during effective-permission computation.

roles.name: Authenticated
roles.description: Special system role — any logged-in user. Base permissions for all authenticated users.

nfrs.name: Security-critical permission flagging
nfrs.statement: Security-critical permissions catalogue explicitly flags permissions allowing privilege elevation; should be assigned with caution. Categories flagged: Content Type Management, Role Management, User Management, Deployment, Workflows, Templates.

nfrs.name: Admin role permission immutability
nfrs.statement: Admin role permission changes are locked — no claims are added or removed via the Edit Role screen. The admin role no longer registers permission-based claims by default; has_permission filter recommended over claim inspection.

nfrs.name: Timing-attack normalization on login
nfrs.statement: When the user is not found during login, a dummy hash verification normalizes response time before returning the invalid-credentials message, preventing username enumeration by timing.

nfrs.name: External authentication rate limiting
nfrs.statement: Rate limiting for external authentication is configured by ExternalAuthenticationRateLimitsStartup.ConfigureServices.

nfrs.name: Security headers configurability
nfrs.statement: Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy (default: no-referrer), and Permissions-Policy headers are configurable from Security → Settings → Security Headers or from application configuration.

nfrs.name: Multi-instance authentication ticket storage
nfrs.statement: Authentication tickets are stored in distributed cache when the Redis feature is enabled, enabling multi-instance deployment support.

nfrs.name: System-type content parts structural integrity
nfrs.statement: IContentDefinitionHandler: system-type parts injected cannot be removed or modified via UI or recipes — structural integrity protection.

nfrs.name: API serialization correctness
nfrs.statement: API serialization is on System.Text.Json with dedicated output formatters for YesSql documents and content entities via Minimal API or ApiController for correctness.

nfrs.name: Audit trail
nfrs.statement: AuditTrailPart attaches change history to content items as a first-class concern — supports compliance and auditability.

nfrs.name: Content version pruning safety
nfrs.statement: Content version pruning: potential unbounded data growth if no content type is selected (nothing is pruned). RetentionDays and VersionsToKeep constrained to minimum 0. Requires operator attention.

nfrs.name: Failed operation atomicity
nfrs.statement: Failed role create/clone/edit operations call ISession.CancelAsync() to prevent partial writes. DataMigrationManager: CancelAsync on exception; finally always calls SaveAsync.

nfrs.name: Background task distributed locking
nfrs.statement: Background task distributed lock prevents concurrent execution per tenant per task. TryAcquireBackgroundTaskLockAsync must succeed; if not: log 'Timeout to acquire a lock', terminate shell scope, break.

nfrs.name: MissingFeaturesByRole permission preservation
nfrs.statement: MissingFeaturesByRole map retains permission assignments for features not currently installed, preserving role configuration across feature enable/disable cycles.

nfrs.name: CI build quality gates
nfrs.statement: Build runs in release configuration; warnings are treated as errors; static analyzers run on every build. Documentation-only changes do not trigger tests.

nfrs.name: Cross-platform unit testing
nfrs.statement: Unit tests run on Ubuntu and Windows agents on every CI push; macOS is covered by manually triggered workflow. A failing test fails the pipeline.

nfrs.name: Authentication and authorisation
nfrs.reason: Every admin action and content management operation requires authentication and role-based authorization; OWASP Top 10 input validation applies to all forms.
nfrs.statement: All admin panel routes require an authenticated session with appropriate permissions; unauthorized requests return Forbid; unauthenticated requests redirect to Login. Input validation applied on all form submissions.

nfrs.name: Privacy of personal data
nfrs.reason: User entity holds PII (email, phone number, username); must comply with data protection obligations.
nfrs.statement: Personal data (email, phone number, username) is stored securely; passwords are stored as hashes; PII is not logged in plaintext.

nfrs.name: Page response performance
nfrs.reason: Admin screens must load within acceptable time limits; modular architecture with per-tenant background polling requires bounded latency.
nfrs.statement: Admin panel pages must render within 2 seconds under normal load; background service PollingTime default 00:01:00 and MinimumIdleTime default 00:00:10 bound task overhead.

nfrs.name: Availability
nfrs.reason: Multi-tenant CMS serving production sites requires high availability.
nfrs.statement: The application must support multi-instance deployment (enabled by Redis distributed cache); each tenant's background tasks run independently with lock-based coordination.

nfrs.name: Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)
nfrs.reason: Admin UI and public-facing registration/login screens must be accessible to users with disabilities.
nfrs.statement: All screens must meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Form fields must have labels; error messages must be screen-reader accessible; focus management required for slide-in forms and modals.

nfrs.name: Browser and device support
nfrs.reason: Admin prototype is a web application; browser support must be defined.
nfrs.statement: The admin panel must support the latest two versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari on desktop. Registration and login screens must be usable on mobile browsers.

nfrs.name: Data retention
nfrs.reason: Content versions and audit trail records accumulate; retention policy prevents unbounded growth.
nfrs.statement: Content version retention is governed by ContentVersionPruningSettings (RetentionDays, VersionsToKeep) per content type. Settings must be configured for all content types to prevent unbounded data growth.

nfrs.name: Backup and recovery
nfrs.reason: YesSql data store and App_Data directory hold all application state; loss requires recovery capability.
nfrs.statement: Regular backups of the YesSql database and App_Data directory must be performed. Recovery procedures must restore all tenant data and configuration.

nfrs.name: Observability — logging and monitoring
nfrs.reason: Background processing, deployment, and migration failures need to be observable; CI browser-test artefacts need capture.
nfrs.statement: Application logs must capture background task execution, migration errors, deployment operations, and authentication events. Browser test artefacts (logs, traces) must be uploaded on failure and retained for post-mortem.

platform.name: Project setup
platform.reason: The codebase is a modular ASP.NET Core application; every module requires a project file (OrchardCore.YourModule.csproj), Manifest.cs, Startup.cs. The local development environment must run before any feature can be built.

platform.name: Data foundation
platform.description: YesSql data store provisioned; schema created via DataMigrationManager (Create method on first run); seed data applied (roles, content types, users, features, tenants, queries).

platform.name: Delivery pipeline
platform.description: CI/CD pipeline in GitHub Actions; release configuration; warnings as errors; analyzers run; unit tests on Ubuntu and Windows; documentation-only changes skip tests; browser tests with Playwright.

platform.name: Test harness
platform.description: Unit and integration tests (xUnit) on Ubuntu/Windows; browser-based functional tests with Playwright (Chromium); emulated cloud services (LocalStack for AWS, Azure fixtures for blob/data-lake); App_Data cleaned between runs; artefacts (logs, traces) uploaded on failure.

platform.name: Login / SSO
platform.description: ASP.NET Core Identity with local username/password login; external OAuth2/OIDC providers (Microsoft Azure AD, Google, Facebook, Twitter/X, GitHub, OpenID Connect); configurable 2FA; local login can be disabled to force external.

platform.name: Roles and permissions
platform.description: Role-based authorization via RolesPermissionsHandler; system roles (Administrator, Anonymous, Authenticated) protected; per-feature permission registration; security-critical permission flagging; implied permissions; full-replace permission save.

platform.name: Audit log
platform.description: AuditTrailPart attaches change history to content items. Audit signals on content create/update/delete operations.

platform.name: Notifications
platform.description: Email notifications via Azure Communication Services Email (verification emails, password reset). SMS notifications via Azure Communication Services SMS. Gated by ManageEmailSettings / ManageSmsSettings permissions.

platform.name: Admin and configuration
platform.description: Admin panel gated by AccessAdminPanel permission; fine-grained menu visibility via ViewAdminMenu_[MenuName] and ViewAdminMenuAll; Security Settings screen for global configuration; Features Administration for module enable/disable.

platform.name: Search
platform.description: Lucene full-text search (in-process) and Elasticsearch (external) with custom token filters and analyzers. Named query API for structured queries (Lucene, SQL, GraphQL).

platform.name: Import/export
platform.description: Deployment Plans with typed steps export/import content definitions, content items, queries, roles. Import/Export permissions are security-critical. Remote Deployment to other Orchard instances.

platform.name: Retention
platform.description: Content version pruning via ContentVersionPruningSettings (RetentionDays, VersionsToKeep per content type). When no content type is selected, nothing is pruned.

platform.name: Error handling
platform.description: XML-RPC exception handling: XRpcFault(0, e.Message); 500 on non-core exceptions. DataMigrationManager: per-feature exception catch, log error, continue. Admin routes: Forbid on missing permission; NotFound for missing items.

platform.name: Logging and monitoring
platform.description: Background task execution logged (success, 'Timeout to acquire a lock'). AutoSetup logs success. Browser test artefacts (logs, traces) uploaded on failure. CI caches Playwright browsers.

platform.name: Security and privacy
platform.description: Timing-attack normalization on login. Configurable security headers (CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy). Rate limiting for external authentication. Admin role is system role — permission-based claims not registered by default. System roles cannot be deleted.

platform.name: Accessibility
platform.reason: The application has a web admin UI and public-facing registration/login screens; WCAG 2.1 AA compliance is required.

platform.name: Performance
platform.reason: Multi-tenant application with background tasks and content indexing needs page-response and throughput targets.

platform.name: Multi-tenant support
platform.description: Tenant Administration for creating, editing, and provisioning tenants. AutoSetup provisions Default tenant on first request. Each tenant has isolated database connection, table prefix, or schema.

rules.name: Last enabled administrator guard
rules.statement: At least one enabled administrator account must always exist. Disabling is blocked when enabledUsersOfAdminRole.Count == 1 && user.UserName == enabledUsersOfAdminRole.First().
rules.message: Cannot disable this user This is the last remaining enabled administrator account. At least one enabled administrator is required.

rules.name: System roles cannot be deleted
rules.statement: System roles (Administrator, Anonymous, Authenticated) cannot be deleted. IsSystemRoleAsync = true → deletion aborts.

rules.name: Role name must not contain /
rules.statement: A role name must not contain the / character.
rules.message: Validation error Role name must not contain / or duplicate an existing role.

rules.name: Role name must be unique
rules.statement: A role name must not duplicate an existing role name.
rules.message: Validation error Role name must not contain / or duplicate an existing role.

rules.name: Admin role permissions are immutable
rules.statement: When editing the admin role, no permission claims are added or removed regardless of submitted selections. IsAdminRoleAsync = true → skip claim changes on EditPost.
rules.message: Admin role permissions are managed by the system Permission assignments for the admin role cannot be modified here.

rules.name: Permission persistence is full-replace
rules.statement: On save, all existing permission claims for a role are removed and replaced with the freshly selected set. Selections: form keys prefixed with Checkbox., value must be 'true'.

rules.name: Content item Title is required
rules.statement: A value is required for Title when saving or publishing a content item.
rules.message: Validation errors A value is required for Title.

rules.name: Tags/Categories restricted to leaf terms
rules.statement: The Tags / Categories chip input is restricted to leaf terms only; multiple selections are allowed.
rules.message: Select leaf terms only. Multiple selections allowed.

rules.name: Priority Level numeric range
rules.statement: Priority Level must be a number with minimum 1 and maximum 10.

rules.name: Content item lifecycle: Remove does not delete
rules.statement: Remove clears Latest and Published flags on the content item without physically deleting the record. Removed items can be restored.

rules.name: Content versioning options
rules.statement: VersionOptions.Published (default): create and publish immediately. VersionOptions.Draft: use existing draft if found, else create new. VersionOptions.DraftRequired: always create a new draft.

rules.name: ContentDefinitionService name validation
rules.statement: Rejects empty display names (IsNullOrWhiteSpace(displayName)). Rejects empty names (IsNullOrWhiteSpace(name)). Name must start with ASCII letter (!char.IsAsciiLetter(name[0])). Name normalized via ToSafeName(). Guards against duplicate definitions.

rules.name: Content type DisplayName max length
rules.statement: ContentTypeDefinition DisplayName is required; not null/not empty; maximum 1,024 characters.

rules.name: System-defined fields cannot be removed
rules.statement: IsSystemDefined = true → disabled Remove button with tooltip 'system-defined fields cannot be removed'.

rules.name: Edit link shown only for recognized field types
rules.statement: Edit link for a content part field is shown only when the field's type appears in registered ContentFieldOptions.

rules.name: Content part field ordering
rules.statement: Fields are ordered by numeric Position from ContentPartFieldSettings; default '0'; ordered field names emitted as hidden inputs (OrderedFieldNames).

rules.name: Default tenant must always be provided
rules.statement: Root tenant ShellName must be 'Default'. Other values fail with the default-tenant error.
rules.message: Validation error The single 'Default' tenant should be provided.

rules.name: Tenant name: letters only, no spaces
rules.statement: AutoSetup ShellName must contain letters only and no spaces.

rules.name: Database connection string required for non-Sqlite
rules.statement: DatabaseConnectionString is required for non-Sqlite database providers.

rules.name: Site time zone required in AutoSetup
rules.statement: SiteTimeZone is required in AutoSetup; omitting fails provisioning.

rules.name: Feature enable/disable force flag
rules.statement: Enable force=true: enable dependencies if required, else fail. Disable force=true: disable dependent features if required, else fail. Default force=false.

rules.name: External Authentication feature auto-enable
rules.statement: External Authentication feature is automatically enabled when a dependent feature is activated; cannot be manually toggled.

rules.name: ContentVersionPruningSettings minimum values
rules.statement: RetentionDays and VersionsToKeep are constrained to minimum 0. When no content type is selected, nothing is pruned.
rules.message: when no content type is selected, nothing is pruned

rules.name: ContentDefinitionDeploymentStep part validation
rules.statement: ContentDefinitionDeploymentStep validates that a part belongs to the selected content type before including it, matching parts by name.

rules.name: Query null guard
rules.statement: QueryGlobalMethodProvider: if query == null, the method does not proceed.

rules.name: Taxonomy field required/unique/leaves-only rules
rules.statement: Taxonomy field: Required — field is required when setting is enabled. Unique — when Unique disabled, multiple selections are permitted. LeavesOnly — when enabled, only leaf terms are selectable.

rules.name: Required text field rejection
rules.statement: Required text fields are rejected when value is empty or whitespace only.

rules.name: CreateContentTask publish decision
rules.statement: CreateContentTask: publish-on-create checked → publishes item immediately; unchecked → creates draft.

rules.name: PublishContentTask and UpdateContentTask expression branching
rules.statement: PublishContentTask and UpdateContentTask branch on whether content expression is empty or whitespace: empty → use default content; set → evaluate expression.

rules.name: UserTaskEventContentDriver gating
rules.statement: Submitted action must start with prefix 'user-task.'; must be among available actions for the activity; activity state must exist in workflow state; when activity defines one or more roles, acting user must belong to at least one; otherwise action is rejected.

rules.name: Rule evaluation requires at least one condition
rules.statement: A rule is evaluated only when it contains at least one condition (Conditions.Count > 0). Each child condition is evaluated by its matching evaluator; if no evaluator or evaluator returns false, condition fails.

rules.name: Anonymous role IsAuthenticated = false
rules.statement: Authentication type left null for Anonymous role so IsAuthenticated = false during effective-permission computation.

rules.name: Implied permission: ViewRoles implied by ManageRoles
rules.statement: ViewRoles is declared with ManageRoles as an implied grant. ManageRoles is marked security-critical.

rules.name: Permission gathering: only enabled features contribute
rules.statement: GetInstalledPermissionsAsync iterates all registered IPermissionProvider; only providers whose feature is enabled contribute. Permissions bucketed under PermissionGroupKey derived from explicit category or feature name/id. Duplicate permission names flagged.
rules.message: Duplicate permissions detected Some permissions with the same name are defined by multiple features. These are flagged below.

rules.name: Registration self-service disabled by default
rules.statement: By default only administrators create accounts; self-service registration requires enabling the Users Registration feature.

rules.name: Registration email verification requires email provider
rules.statement: When email verification is enabled, new users must verify their email address before they can log in; this requires a configured email provider.
rules.message: Please verify your email address before logging in. Check your inbox for a verification link.

rules.name: ManageRecipes permission replaces SiteOwner
rules.statement: ManageRecipes permission gates recipe execution, replacing the deprecated SiteOwner permission.

rules.name: DataMigrationManager idempotency
rules.statement: UpdateAsync is idempotent — skips features in _processedFeatures. current == 0 → run Create; otherwise walk upgrade lookup table.

rules.name: XML-RPC exception fault format
rules.statement: If core exception raised, report error message via XRpcFault(0, e.Message); otherwise signal a 500.

rules.name: Upgrade-time admin role security caveat
rules.statement: A role assigned with no permissions may cause users in that role to be automatically granted the Administrator role during upgrade; administrators must verify and remove the admin role from any account that should not have it.

rules.name: Login: local login disabled check
rules.statement: When local login is disabled in security settings, sign-in is blocked immediately with the local-disabled message.

rules.name: Login: user not enabled
rules.statement: A user whose status is Disabled is denied sign-in even if the password check passes.
rules.message: The specified user is not allowed to sign in.

rules.name: Login: user lookup order
rules.statement: User lookup resolves by user name first; falls back to email when identity options require a unique email.

rules.name: Admin menu gating
rules.statement: AccessAdminPanel permission gates the admin panel. ViewAdminMenu_[MenuName] and ViewAdminMenuAll control fine-grained menu item visibility.

rules.name: Content permissions: own vs others scope
rules.statement: Content permissions distinguish 'own' vs 'others' scopes: EditOwnContent vs EditContent, PublishOwnContent vs PublishContent.

rules.name: Confidential OAuth clients require a secret
rules.statement: Confidential identity clients require a secret; a client without a secret is rejected.

glossary.definition: The data persistence layer used by Orchard Core; a document/relational ORM that stores data in SQL databases with map/reduce indexing.

Defines the structure of a content type: DisplayName (max 1024 chars), Name (must start with ASCII letter, normalized via ToSafeName, unique), Parts collection, Settings JSON, and behaviour toggles (Creatable, Listable, Draftable, Versionable, Securable).
Defines a single field within a content part: Name (string), field type, position, IsSystemDefined flag, and Settings JSON.
Defines a reusable field type (e.g. TextField, DateField) that can be attached to content parts.
Carries generic settings associated with content metadata on a content type or item.
Attaches localization data to content items for multi-culture content; implements ILocalizable interface.
A content part that attaches change history as a first-class concern; carries audit operation signals; supports compliance and auditability.
Content parts that support previewing content before it is published; uses PreviewPartViewModel and contentpreview.edit client script.
Per content type settings controlling version retention: RetentionDays (minimum 0) and VersionsToKeep (minimum 0). When no content type is selected, nothing is pruned.
Enum controlling content item versioning: Published (create + publish immediately), Draft (use existing draft or create new), DraftRequired (always create new draft).

A typed step in a Deployment Plan. Types: ContentDefinitionDeploymentStep, DeleteContentDefinitionDeploymentStep, ContentItemDeploymentStep, AllContentDeploymentStep, QueryBasedContentDeploymentStep, AllQueriesDeploymentStep, ExportContentToDeploymentTargetDeploymentStep, AllRolesDeploymentStep.
Configuration for sitemap generation: Mode ('index all' or 'limit items'); SelectedContentTypes (optional, restricts indexing by display name).
Configuration for administrative navigation: Mode ('show all' or restricted set of selected content types).
Reads and saves Azure Active Directory / Microsoft Entra ID configuration; carries a token security signal.
YesSql document storing the full list of roles and the MissingFeaturesByRole map (permissions referencing absent features).
A map in RolesDocument that retains permission assignments referencing features not currently installed, preserving role configuration across feature enable/disable cycles.
Per-feature version record used by DataMigrationManager to track the current schema version; created if absent.

Coordinates schema evolution across all tenants and features. Runs Create on version 0; walks upgrade lookup table otherwise. Idempotent (skips _processedFeatures). Cancels session on exception; always saves in finally.

An ASP.NET Core BackgroundService that polls running tenants on a fixed interval (PollingTime, default 00:01:00) under a distributed lock (TryAcquireBackgroundTaskLockAsync). MinimumIdleTime default 00:00:10.
Context passed to background task event handlers: taskName, scope, Exception (set on non-fatal error).
Represents an installed module: IExtensionInfo Descriptor, NeedsVersionUpdate, IsRecentlyInstalled, CanUninstall, Notifications (List<string>).
Feature flag: feature is always enabled and cannot be disabled (e.g. OrchardCore.Features).
Feature flag: feature has a pending schema migration or configuration update.
Feature flag: feature was installed in the current session or recently.
Feature flag: feature was enabled automatically as a dependency of another feature, not by direct user action.
Feature flag: feature requires a version-level update.

Mechanism that provisions the Default tenant on the first HTTP request using configuration values (no browser wizard required). Triggers only on uninitialized App_Data; requires SiteTimeZone and DatabaseProvider.
Optional configuration: empty → AutoSetup triggers on any request; if set must start with /.
A named setup script applied during site or tenant provisioning. Available options: Blog, Headless, Agency, Blank.
The key used to bucket permissions in the Edit Role screen; derived from explicit category or feature name/id.
A normalization function applied to content type and content part names to ensure they are valid identifiers.
XML-RPC MetaWeblog protocol handler under OrchardCore.Lists; authorization-gated; raises XRpcFault on exception.
XML-RPC fault object constructed as XRpcFault(0, e.Message) when a core exception is caught in the XML-RPC HomeController.
Resolves IQueryManager via DI, locates named query, null-guards, and executes the query. Used for Liquid template query execution.
Deployment step that exports all roles as part of a deployment package for environment-to-environment migration.
Interface providing TryAcquireBackgroundTaskLockAsync for per-task locking in the background service.
Configuration key in appsettings.json for overriding the default Administrator role name.
Content type behaviour toggle: whether instances of this type can be created through the UI.
Content type behaviour toggle: whether instances appear in list views.
Content type behaviour toggle: whether draft versions are permitted for this content type.
Content type behaviour toggle: whether version history is retained for this content type.
Content type behaviour toggle: whether instance-level permissions apply to this content type.
Required file for every Orchard Core module; describes the module's metadata (id, name, category, dependencies).
Interface implemented by each module to register its permissions with the system; only providers whose feature is enabled contribute to the permission grid.
Permission that gates access to the entire admin panel.
Permission that gates recipe execution; replaces the deprecated SiteOwner permission.
Content permissions scoped to items the current user authored, as distinct from EditContent / PublishContent which apply to all items.

Configuration object for AutoSetup provisioning: ShellName, SiteName, AdminUsername, AdminEmail, AdminPassword, DatabaseProvider, RecipeName, SiteTimeZone (required), DatabaseConnectionString (required for non-Sqlite), DatabaseTablePrefix (optional), DatabaseSchema (optional), RequestUrlHost, RequestUrlPrefix, FeatureProfile.
YesSql session methods: CancelAsync rolls back pending changes on exception; SaveAsync persists changes. Pattern: CancelAsync on exception, SaveAsync in finally.

stories.title: Sign in with local credentials
stories.i_want: to sign in to the application using my username or email address and password
stories.so_that: I can access my personalised account and protected features
stories.description: Provides the Login page with a local credential form. On successful submission the application authenticates the user and redirects to the administration dashboard. Remember Me extends the session duration. Google and Microsoft OAuth buttons initiate external authentication flows handled by other endpoints.
preconditions: The application is running and the Login page is reachable
Local login is enabled in the security settings

requirements.text: The system shall display the Login page with a Username or email text field, a Password password field, a Remember me checkbox, a Sign in action, a Create one link, a Google action, and a Microsoft action.
When the user submits the login form with a recognised username or email and a matching password, the system shall authenticate the user and redirect to the administration dashboard.
When the user submits the login form with valid credentials and Remember me selected, the system shall issue an authentication token with an extended expiry period.
The system shall resolve a submitted identifier by matching on username first, falling back to email address when the identity configuration requires a unique email.
When the user activates the Google action on the Login page, the system shall redirect the browser to the Google OAuth consent screen.
When the user activates the Microsoft action on the Login page, the system shall redirect the browser to the Microsoft Azure AD / Entra ID consent screen.

When the user submits the login form with invalid credentials for the 3rd time within 15 minutes, the system shall lock the account for 15 minutes and display the message "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." on the Login page.

stories.description: The Users Administration page presents a paginated table of all user accounts. The administrator can filter by status (Enabled or Disabled) and search by username or email. The list is backed by GET /v1/users and is restricted to callers holding the ManageUsers permission.
preconditions: The administrator has a valid authenticated session.
The administrator holds the ManageUsers permission.

requirements.text: When an administrator navigates to the Users Administration page, the system shall call GET /v1/users and display the returned user accounts in a paginated list.
The system shall support pagination of the user list via limit and offset query parameters, with a default page size of 20.
When the administrator selects a status filter value, the system shall pass the chosen status as a query parameter to GET /v1/users and display only the matching user accounts.
When the administrator enters a search term, the system shall pass the term as a search query parameter to GET /v1/users and display only users whose username or email matches.
If the request to list users is made without a valid session, then the system shall reject the request with HTTP 401 and the message "Authentication required."
If the authenticated caller does not hold the ManageUsers permission, then the system shall reject the list-users request with HTTP 403 and the message "Insufficient permissions."

stories.i_want: to create a new user account from the admin panel
stories.so_that: I can provision access for new team members with the appropriate roles and status
stories.description: The administrator opens the create-user slide-in form from the Users Administration page, fills in username, email, phone number, password, status and roles, then saves. The server validates uniqueness and format and returns specific error messages when validation fails. The form also shows an inline validation-errors panel for 400 and 409 responses.

The administrator holds the ManageUsers permission.
The Users Administration page is open.

requirements.text: When the administrator clicks the Create user button, the system shall display the create-user slide-in form containing fields for username, email, phone number, password, password confirmation, status, roles and a Send welcome email option.
When the administrator clicks the Cancel / close form button, the system shall hide the create-user slide-in form without saving any data.
When the administrator submits the create-user form with valid data, the system shall call POST /v1/users, create the user account, and return the new user's id and username with HTTP status 201.
If the submitted username is already in use, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 409 and show "Username is already taken."
If the submitted username contains invalid characters, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 400 and show "Username contains invalid characters."
If the submitted email address is already registered, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 409 and show "Email address is already registered."
If the submitted email address is not in valid format, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 400 and show "Email address is invalid."
If the create-user request is made without a valid session, then the system shall reject the request with HTTP 401 and the message "Authentication required."
If the caller lacks the ManageUsers permission when submitting the create-user form, then the system shall reject the request with HTTP 403 and the message "Insufficient permissions."
When the administrator submits the create-user form with the Send welcome email option enabled, the system shall send an email to the new user's address containing a link to set their password.

stories.title: Update User Account (Admin)
stories.i_want: to update a user's account details, status, and role assignments from the admin panel
stories.so_that: user accounts remain accurate and correctly configured as roles and information change
stories.description: An administrator with EditUsers permission updates any combination of a user's username, email address, phone number, account status, and role assignments via PUT /v1/users/{userId}. The system validates uniqueness and format constraints, returning per-field messages on failure. Only supplied fields are changed.
preconditions: The caller is authenticated as an administrator with the EditUsers permission.
The target user account exists in the system.

requirements.text: When an administrator submits an update request for an existing user with valid field values, the system shall save the updated fields and return HTTP 200 with the user id and username.
The system shall accept partial updates to the username, email, phoneNumber, status, and roles fields of a user account, applying changes only to the fields supplied in the request.
If the submitted username is already taken by another account, then the system shall reject the update and return HTTP 400 with "Validation errors • Username is already taken".
If the submitted username contains invalid characters, then the system shall reject the update and return HTTP 400 with "Validation errors • Username contains invalid characters".
If the submitted email address is already registered to another account, then the system shall reject the update and return HTTP 400 with "Validation errors • Email address is already registered".

stories.title: Clone Role
stories.i_want: to clone an existing role under a new name, inheriting all its permissions
stories.so_that: I can quickly create variant roles based on an existing configuration without starting from scratch
stories.description: Provides the Clone Role screen and POST /v1/roles/{roleName}/clone endpoint. The Administrator specifies a new role name; the system copies the source role with all its permissions under the new name. The new name must not contain / and must not duplicate an existing role name. Cancelling navigates back to the roles list without saving.
preconditions: The Administrator is authenticated with the ManageRoles permission
At least one non-system role exists to serve as the clone source
The Administrator has navigated to the Clone Role screen for the source role

requirements.text: When the Administrator submits the Clone Role form with a valid new role name, the system shall clone the source role with all its permissions under the new name via POST /v1/roles/{roleName}/clone and navigate to the roles list.
The system shall copy all permissions of the source role to the cloned role during a Clone Role operation.
If the New role name field is empty when the Clone Role form is submitted, then the system shall refuse the submission and indicate that the New role name field is required.
If the new role name contains the / character, then the system shall refuse the clone and show "Validation error Role name must not contain / or duplicate an existing role."
If the new role name duplicates an existing role name, then the system shall refuse the clone and show "Validation error Role name must not contain / or duplicate an existing role."
When the Administrator clicks Cancel on the Clone Role screen, the system shall navigate to the roles list without saving.
If the POST /v1/roles/{roleName}/clone request carries no valid session, then the system shall return HTTP 401 with code UNAUTHORIZED and message "Authentication required."

If the POST /v1/roles/{roleName}/clone request is made by a caller lacking the ManageRoles permission, then the system shall return HTTP 403 with code FORBIDDEN and message "Insufficient permissions."
If the source roleName in POST /v1/roles/{roleName}/clone does not exist, then the system shall return HTTP 404 with code ROLE_NOT_FOUND and message "Role not found."
When POST /v1/roles/{roleName}/clone receives a valid request, the system shall return HTTP 201 with the new role id and name.

stories.title: Edit Role Permissions
stories.i_want: to view and update the permission assignments for a custom role using a checklist
stories.so_that: I can precisely control what actions members of that role are authorised to perform
stories.description: The administrator opens the Edit Role screen for a custom role, reviews the current permission selections across all available permission checkboxes, makes changes, and saves. The save operation is a full-replace: all existing permission claims are removed and replaced with exactly the submitted selection (BR-06). The admin role is protected by BR-05 and its permissions cannot be modified; the screen enters a locked state with an informational message.
preconditions: The administrator is authenticated and holds the ManageRoles permission.
The target role exists in the system.

requirements.text: When the administrator opens the Edit Role screen for a role, the system shall fetch and display the role's current permission selections.
The system shall present each available permission as a labelled checkbox on the Edit Role screen.
When the administrator submits the Edit Role form, the system shall replace all existing permission claims of the role with exactly the submitted selection.

While the role being edited is the admin role, the system shall display "Admin role permissions are managed by the system Permission assignments for the admin role cannot be modified here." and prevent saving.
If API-19 returns VALIDATION_ERROR, then the system shall refuse the save and display "Validation error Unable to save role changes."

If duplicate permission names are detected across installed features, then the system shall flag the affected permissions and display "Duplicate permissions detected Some permissions with the same name are defined by multiple features. These are flagged below."
When the administrator clicks "Back to roles", the system shall navigate to the roles list screen.

stories.i_want: to browse and filter content items in the admin list
stories.so_that: I can locate and manage the content I am responsible for
stories.description: The Content Admin List screen provides a filterable, paginated view of all content items backed by API-22. Users apply Search, Content Type, Status, and Author filters to narrow the list. An empty-state message is shown when no items match. From this screen users navigate to create a new item or open an existing item for editing.

The user holds the ViewContent permission

requirements.text: When the content admin list page is opened, the system shall request GET /v1/content-items and display the returned items in a paginated table.
When a user enters a term in the Search field and submits, the system shall pass the term as the search query parameter to GET /v1/content-items and refresh the list.
When a user selects a value from the Content type dropdown, the system shall pass the selected value as the contentType query parameter to GET /v1/content-items and refresh the list.
When a user selects a value from the Status dropdown, the system shall pass the selected value as the status query parameter to GET /v1/content-items and refresh the list.
When a user enters a name in the Author field and submits, the system shall pass the name as the author query parameter to GET /v1/content-items and refresh the list.
If no content items match the applied filters, the system shall display the message "No items match your filter criteria Try adjusting your search or filter parameters".
When a user clicks Create new, the system shall navigate to the content item editor in create mode.
When a user clicks Edit on a content item row, the system shall navigate to the content item editor for that item.
If the caller has no valid session when GET /v1/content-items is called, the system shall return HTTP 401 with code UNAUTHORIZED and message "Authentication required."
If the caller lacks the ViewContent permission when GET /v1/content-items is called, the system shall return HTTP 403 with code FORBIDDEN and message "Insufficient permissions."

If a user holding only EditOwnContent permission attempts to edit a content item authored by another user, the system shall refuse the action and return HTTP 403.
If a user holding only PublishOwnContent permission attempts to publish a content item authored by another user, the system shall refuse the action and return HTTP 403.

stories.title: Load Existing Content Item into Editor
stories.i_want: to open an existing content item in the Content Item Editor with its current field values loaded
stories.so_that: I can review its publication status and begin editing
stories.description: When a user navigates to the Content Item Editor for an existing content item, the system fetches the item via GET /v1/content-items/{contentItemId}, selecting the appropriate version per BR-11 (Published by default, Draft, or Latest), and renders all editable fields. A status indicator shows whether the item is Draft or Published. From the editor the user can cancel to return to the list or preview the rendered content.
preconditions: User is authenticated
User holds the ViewContent permission

requirements.text: When an editor opens the Content Item Editor for an existing content item, the system shall call GET /v1/content-items/{contentItemId} to retrieve the item's current field values.

While the Content Item Editor is open with an existing content item loaded, the system shall display all editable fields: Title, Body Text, Priority Level, Featured, Publication Date, Related Link, Custom HTML, Tags / Categories, Notes (Markdown), Featured Image, and Related Content.
The system shall support a version query parameter accepting Published (default), Draft, or Latest when retrieving a content item, in accordance with BR-11 versioning options.
While a content item has Draft status, the system shall display the state indicator "Draft Not yet published" in the Content Item Editor.
While a content item has Published status, the system shall display the state indicator "Published Live" in the Content Item Editor.
If the requested content item does not exist, then the system shall display "Content not found The requested content item does not exist."
If the caller lacks ViewContent permission, then the system shall display "Access denied You do not have permission to edit this content item."
When the editor activates the Cancel action, the system shall navigate to the content admin list without saving any changes.
When the editor activates the Preview action, the system shall navigate to the content display screen for the current content item.

If the caller lacks EditContent permission when activating Save Draft, then the system shall refuse the save and display "Access denied You do not have permission to edit this content item."

stories.title: Publish a Content Item
stories.i_want: to publish a content item so it becomes live
stories.so_that: readers can view the content on the site
stories.description: An authenticated user with PublishContent permission triggers the publish action on a content item from the admin list or the content editor. The item transitions to Published status and downstream integrations are notified. The operation is idempotent.
preconditions: The user is authenticated with a valid session.
The user holds the PublishContent permission (ROL-01 or ROL-02).
The target content item exists.

requirements.text: When an authenticated user with PublishContent permission submits a publish request for a content item, the system shall transition the content item to Published status and return the updated contentItemId and status.
When a publish request is received for a content item that is already Published, the system shall return the current Published status without creating a new version.
If a publish request is made without a valid session, then the system shall refuse the request and return "Authentication required."
If the caller lacks the PublishContent permission, then the system shall refuse the publish request and return "Access denied You do not have permission to edit this content item."
If the contentItemId supplied in the publish request does not exist, then the system shall refuse the request and return "Content not found The requested content item does not exist."
When a content item is successfully published, the system shall invoke the INT-05 integration to notify downstream consumers of the publication event.
When a content item is successfully published, the system shall invoke the INT-06 integration as required by the post-publish workflow.
The system shall enforce BR-11 when processing a publish request for a content item.
The system shall enforce BR-45 when processing a publish request for a content item.

requirements.text: When the administrator activates the Remove action for a field with isSystemDefined equal to false, the system shall delete the field via DELETE /v1/content-types/{typeName}/fields/{fieldName} and remove the field from the displayed list.

If the request to remove a field targets a field with isSystemDefined equal to true, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 422 and return the message "system-defined fields cannot be removed".

If the caller lacks the EditContentTypes permission, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 403 and return the message "Insufficient permissions."
If no valid session exists, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 401 and return the message "Authentication required."

While the Site Setup page is displayed, the system shall populate the Site time zone dropdown with valid IANA time zone identifiers including UTC, America/New_York, America/Chicago, America/Denver, America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London, Europe/Paris, Asia/Tokyo, Asia/Shanghai, and Australia/Sydney.

If the POST /v1/setup response status is 409 with code ALREADY_SETUP, then the system shall display "Site is already set up." and prevent further form submission.
If the POST /v1/setup response status is 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR, then the system shall reveal the site-setup--validation-error panel and display "Please check your input".

stories.i_want: to provision a new tenant by supplying its name, recipe, and database configuration

stories.description: The Administrator submits POST /v1/tenants. The system validates the name (letters only, unique, root must be Default), recipe (one of Blog|Headless|Agency|Blank), and database connection string (required when provider is not Sqlite). On success the tenant is created with status Uninitialized. Rules BR-17, BR-18, and BR-19 govern the name constraints and root-tenant rule.
preconditions: The caller holds an active session with the ManageTenants permission (ROL-01).

requirements.text: When an authenticated user with the ManageTenants permission sends POST /v1/tenants with a valid name, recipe, and database configuration, the system shall provision the tenant and return HTTP 201 with the tenant name and status Uninitialized.
The system shall set every newly created tenant's initial status to Uninitialized.

If the supplied tenant name contains non-letter characters or spaces, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 400 with code INVALID_NAME and message "Tenant name must contain letters only and no spaces."

If the root tenant name provided is not Default, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and message "Validation error The single 'Default' tenant should be provided."

If the supplied tenant name is already in use by an existing tenant, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 409 with code DUPLICATE_TENANT and message "A tenant with this name already exists."

If databaseProvider is not Sqlite and databaseConnectionString is absent, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 400 with a validation error indicating that the connection string is required.
If the supplied recipe is not one of Blog, Headless, Agency, or Blank, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 400 with a validation error indicating an invalid recipe value.
If no valid session exists, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 401 with code UNAUTHORIZED and message "Authentication required."
If the caller lacks the ManageTenants permission, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 403 with code FORBIDDEN and message "Insufficient permissions."

stories.title: Enable a Feature
stories.i_want: to enable a feature by its identifier with the option to force-enable its disabled dependencies
stories.so_that: I can activate module capabilities in the application with minimal manual steps
stories.description: An authenticated administrator calls POST /v1/features/{featureId}/enable to activate a feature. When force=false (default) and one or more required dependencies are disabled, the request is refused with an explanatory error. When force=true, the system enables all disabled dependencies before enabling the target feature. The operation is idempotent: enabling an already-enabled feature returns HTTP 200 without side effects.
preconditions: Administrator holds an active, authenticated session
Administrator has the ManageFeatures permission via ROL-01

requirements.text: When an administrator submits an enable request for a feature whose required dependencies are all already enabled, the system shall enable the feature and return HTTP 200 with the list of enabled feature identifiers and a success message.

When an administrator submits an enable request with force=true, the system shall enable all disabled required dependencies and the target feature and return HTTP 200 with the complete list of enabled feature identifiers.
The system shall treat an enable request that omits the force body parameter as equivalent to force=false.

If force=false and at least one required dependency of the target feature is not enabled, then the system shall refuse the enable request with HTTP 400 and return "Cannot enable feature: required dependencies are not enabled. Use force=true to enable dependencies."
If the enable request is made without a valid session, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 401 and return "Authentication required."
If the caller submitting an enable request lacks the ManageFeatures permission, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 403 and return "Insufficient permissions."
If the featureId in the enable request path does not identify a known feature, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 404 and return "Feature not found."
While a feature is already in the enabled state, the system shall accept a subsequent enable request and return HTTP 200 without modifying any feature state.

stories.title: Disable a Feature
stories.i_want: to disable a feature by its identifier with the option to force-disable its enabled dependents
stories.so_that: I can deactivate module capabilities that are no longer needed without having to manually cascade the operation
stories.description: An authenticated administrator calls POST /v1/features/{featureId}/disable to deactivate a feature. When force=false (default) and one or more dependent features remain enabled, the request is refused with an explanatory error. When force=true, the system disables all enabled dependents before disabling the target feature. The operation is idempotent.
preconditions: Administrator holds an active, authenticated session
Administrator has the ManageFeatures permission via ROL-01

requirements.text: When an administrator submits a disable request for a feature that has no enabled dependents, the system shall disable the feature and return HTTP 200 with the list of disabled feature identifiers and a success message.

When an administrator submits a disable request with force=true, the system shall disable all enabled dependent features and the target feature and return HTTP 200 with the complete list of disabled feature identifiers.
The system shall treat a disable request that omits the force body parameter as equivalent to force=false.

If force=false and at least one dependent feature of the target is still enabled, then the system shall refuse the disable request with HTTP 400 and return "Cannot disable feature: dependent features are still enabled. Use force=true to disable all."
If the disable request is made without a valid session, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 401 and return "Authentication required."
If the caller submitting a disable request lacks the ManageFeatures permission, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 403 and return "Insufficient permissions."
If the featureId in the disable request path does not identify a known feature, then the system shall refuse the request with HTTP 404 and return "Feature not found."
While a feature is already in the disabled state, the system shall accept a subsequent disable request and return HTTP 200 without modifying any feature state.

stories.i_want: External Authentication to be automatically enabled when I activate a feature that depends on it, and for direct manual toggling of that feature to be prevented
stories.so_that: External Authentication is always in the correct state without manual intervention and cannot be accidentally disabled
stories.description: BR-22 mandates that the External Authentication feature is automatically enabled whenever a dependent feature is activated. It cannot be directly enabled or disabled via the Enable Feature or Disable Feature endpoints; any such direct attempt is refused.

Administrator has the ManageFeatures permission via ROL-01
The External Authentication feature exists in the system

requirements.text: When a feature that depends on External Authentication is activated and External Authentication is not already enabled, the system shall automatically enable the External Authentication feature as part of the activation.

If an administrator submits a direct enable request targeting the External Authentication feature identifier, then the system shall refuse the request and indicate that the External Authentication feature cannot be manually toggled.

If an administrator submits a direct disable request targeting the External Authentication feature identifier, then the system shall refuse the request and indicate that the External Authentication feature cannot be manually toggled.

stories.title: Add Deployment Step
stories.i_want: to add a typed step to a deployment plan
stories.so_that: the plan captures the exact operations and configuration needed for deployment
stories.description: An Administrator can append a new step of a recognised type, with optional configuration and position, to an existing deployment plan via POST /v1/deployment-plans/{planId}/steps. The endpoint rejects unknown step types and enforces that ContentDefinitionDeploymentStep parts belong to the selected content type.
preconditions: The administrator is authenticated with a valid session
A deployment plan with the specified planId exists
The caller holds the ManageDeploymentPlan permission

requirements.text: When an authenticated administrator with ManageDeploymentPlan permission submits a valid add-step request for an existing deployment plan, the system shall create the step and return HTTP 201 with the new step id and stepType.

The system shall accept the following stepType values: ContentDefinitionDeploymentStep, DeleteContentDefinitionDeploymentStep, ContentItemDeploymentStep, AllContentDeploymentStep, QueryBasedContentDeploymentStep, AllQueriesDeploymentStep, ExportContentToDeploymentTargetDeploymentStep, and AllRolesDeploymentStep.
If the submitted stepType is not one of the recognised step type values, then the system shall refuse the request and return error code INVALID_STEP_TYPE with message "Step type is invalid."
If the add-step request carries no valid session, then the system shall refuse the request and return error code UNAUTHORIZED with message "Authentication required."
If the caller lacks the ManageDeploymentPlan permission, then the system shall refuse the add-step request and return error code FORBIDDEN with message "Insufficient permissions."

If the planId in the path does not identify an existing deployment plan, then the system shall refuse the add-step request and return error code PLAN_NOT_FOUND with message "Deployment plan not found."

If the stepType is ContentDefinitionDeploymentStep and the specified content part does not belong to the selected content type, then the system shall refuse the request and return error code PART_NOT_IN_TYPE with message "Content part does not belong to the selected content type."

stories.title: Distributed Locking for Background Tasks
stories.i_want: the background service to acquire a distributed lock before executing each task
stories.so_that: each task runs in exactly one service instance at a time, preventing duplicate execution across multiple nodes
stories.description: Before processing any scheduled task, the background service acquires a distributed lock scoped to that task. If the lock is already held, the service skips the cycle and retries at the next polling interval. The lock is released on completion or failure.
preconditions: The background processing module is enabled.

requirements.text: When the background service is ready to execute a scheduled task, the system shall acquire a distributed lock for that task before processing begins.
If the distributed lock for a task cannot be acquired because it is already held by another instance, then the system shall skip that execution cycle and retry at the next polling interval.
When a background task execution completes or terminates with an error, the system shall release the distributed lock for that task.

stories.title: Enforce User Task Action Gating via UserTaskEventContentDriver

stories.i_want: the system to validate my submitted action before processing it

stories.description: The UserTaskEventContentDriver validates every submitted action against four gates: the action name must start with 'user-task.'; the action must be in the activity's available actions list; the activity state must exist in the current workflow state; when the activity restricts access by role the acting user must belong to at least one of those roles.

If the activity state does not exist in the current workflow state, then the system shall reject the action.
While the activity defines one or more roles, the system shall require the acting user to belong to at least one of those roles before processing the action.
If the activity defines one or more roles and the acting user does not belong to any of those roles, then the system shall reject the action.

stories.title: Gate Workflow Rule Evaluation on Minimum Condition Count
stories.i_want: the workflow engine to skip rules that have no conditions and to fail any condition whose evaluator is absent or returns false
stories.so_that: rules are never unintentionally satisfied and evaluation failures are deterministic
stories.description: A rule is evaluated only when it contains at least one condition (Conditions.Count > 0). A rule with zero conditions is skipped entirely. For rules with conditions, each child condition is dispatched to its matching evaluator; a missing evaluator or a false result from the evaluator causes that condition to fail.
preconditions: The administrator is authenticated and authorised to configure workflow rules
A workflow definition contains at least one rule

requirements.text: While a rule contains zero conditions, the system shall skip evaluation of that rule.
When a rule containing at least one condition is evaluated, the system shall pass each child condition to its matching evaluator.
If no matching evaluator exists for a condition, then the system shall treat that condition as failed.
If a condition's evaluator returns false, then the system shall treat that condition as failed.

Given a workflow rule with a condition whose type has no registered evaluator
When the workflow engine evaluates that condition
Then the system shall treat the condition as failed
Scenario: Condition whose evaluator returns false is treated as failed
Given a workflow rule with a condition whose registered evaluator returns false
When the workflow engine evaluates that condition
Then the system shall treat the condition as failed
business_rules: A rule is evaluated only when it contains at least one condition (Conditions.Count > 0). Each child condition is evaluated by its matching evaluator; if no evaluator or evaluator returns false, condition fails.

stories.title: Retrieve a published content item via external REST API
stories.i_want: to retrieve a content item by ID through the external REST Content API
stories.so_that: my headless application or integration client can display or process published content without accessing the CMS directly
stories.description: Provides a GET endpoint at /v1/api/content/{contentItemId} that external integration clients use to fetch a specific content item. Supports Bearer token and API key authentication. Returns the published version by default; supports a version query parameter to request Draft or Latest. Returns structured JSON with contentItemId, title, contentType, and status. Enforces authentication and permission checks and returns standard error responses for missing auth, insufficient permissions, or unknown content.
preconditions: The REST Content API feature is enabled on the tenant.
The caller holds a valid Bearer token or API key.
The target content item exists in the CMS.

requirements.text: When an authenticated GET /v1/api/content/{contentItemId} request is received, the system shall return HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing contentItemId, title, contentType, and status for the matching content item.
When the version query parameter is omitted, the system shall return the published version of the content item by default.
When the version query parameter is set to Draft or Latest, the system shall return the corresponding version of the content item.
The system shall accept both a Bearer token and an API key as valid authentication credentials for the external REST Content API.
If no Bearer token or API key is provided in the request, then the system shall return HTTP 401 with error code UNAUTHORIZED and message "Authentication required."
If the authenticated caller lacks the AccessContentApi or ApiViewContent permission, then the system shall return HTTP 403 with error code FORBIDDEN and message "Insufficient permissions."
If the contentItemId does not exist or is not visible to the caller, then the system shall return HTTP 404 with error code NOT_FOUND and message "Content not found."

stories.title: Create a content item via external REST API
stories.i_want: to create a new content item by posting to the external REST Content API
stories.so_that: my integration system can programmatically publish or draft content without using the CMS editing interface
stories.description: Provides a POST endpoint at /v1/api/content that allows external integration clients to create a new content item. The caller supplies contentType (must reference an existing ContentTypeDefinition), title (required, not empty), and an optional draft flag. On success the API returns HTTP 201 with the new contentItemId and status. Enforces title presence (BR-07) and content versioning options (BR-11). Returns structured validation errors, 401, and 403 on failure. Supports both Bearer token and API key authentication.
preconditions: The REST Content API feature is enabled on the tenant.
The caller holds a valid Bearer token or API key.
The referenced contentType exists as a ContentTypeDefinition.

requirements.text: When an authenticated POST /v1/api/content request is received with a valid title and an existing contentType, the system shall create a new content item and return HTTP 201 with a JSON body containing the new contentItemId and status.
When the draft field is omitted or set to false in the request body, the system shall create the content item in Published status.
When the draft field is set to true in the request body, the system shall create the content item in Draft status.
If the title field is empty or missing, then the system shall return HTTP 400 with error code VALIDATION_ERROR and message "Validation errors A value is required for Title."
If the contentType does not reference an existing ContentTypeDefinition, then the system shall return HTTP 400 with error code VALIDATION_ERROR indicating the content type is invalid.
If no Bearer token or API key is provided in the request, then the system shall return HTTP 401 with error code UNAUTHORIZED and message "Authentication required."
If the authenticated caller lacks the AccessContentApi permission, then the system shall return HTTP 403 with error code FORBIDDEN and message "Insufficient permissions."

stories.description: Implements the POST /v1/xmlrpc endpoint for MetaWeblog XML-RPC remote publishing. Returns a valid XML-RPC method response on success, an XML-RPC fault (XRpcFault(0, e.Message)) on core exceptions per BR-39, and HTTP 500 on non-core exceptions.

If a non-core exception is raised during XML-RPC processing at /v1/xmlrpc, then the system shall return HTTP 500 with error code "INTERNAL_ERROR" and message "Internal server error."

requirements.text: The system shall persist a new Role record containing the attributes id, name, description, isSystemRole, isAdminRole, and isSpecial.

If the submitted role name duplicates an existing Role record name, then the system shall reject the create request and show "Validation error Role name must not contain / or duplicate an existing role.".
When a Role record is successfully created, the system shall write an audit log entry recording the actor identity, timestamp, and the new role name.

The administrator is authenticated

stories.title: Create Content Item (Draft)
stories.i_want: to create a new content item as a draft
stories.so_that: content can be authored and staged before publication
stories.description: Builds the create operation for the ContentItem entity, persisting a new record in Draft status with a unique ID and version, enforcing the mandatory title field, and supporting VersionOptions semantics (Draft, DraftRequired, Published).
preconditions: The Administrator is authenticated.
A valid content type exists in the system.

requirements.text: When a create content item request is received, the system shall persist a new ContentItem record with status set to "Draft", isLatest set to true, and isPublished set to false.
The system shall assign a unique contentItemId and a unique contentItemVersionId to each newly created ContentItem record.
When a new ContentItem is created, the system shall record the modifiedDate as the timestamp of the creation operation.
If the title field is empty or absent on a create content item request, then the system shall refuse the request and show "Validation errors A value is required for Title".
When a create content item request is received with VersionOptions.Draft, the system shall return the existing draft version if one exists, or create a new draft ContentItem if none exists.
When a create content item request is received with VersionOptions.DraftRequired, the system shall always create a new draft ContentItem version.
When a create content item request is received with VersionOptions.Published, the system shall create and publish the ContentItem immediately.

stories.title: Publish and Unpublish Content Item
stories.i_want: to publish a draft content item and to unpublish a published content item
stories.so_that: content visibility is controlled through the ContentItem lifecycle
stories.description: Builds the publish and unpublish lifecycle transitions for ContentItem, updating status, isPublished, and modifiedDate, and enforcing title presence and content-permission scope (own vs. others).
preconditions: The Administrator is authenticated.
A ContentItem exists in the data store.

requirements.text: When a publish request is received for a ContentItem, the system shall set the ContentItem status to "Published", isPublished to true, and modifiedDate to the current timestamp.
The system shall enforce PublishContent or PublishOwnContent permission for every publish request submitted against a ContentItem.
If the requesting user holds only PublishOwnContent permission and the ContentItem author differs from the requesting user, then the system shall refuse the publish request.
When an unpublish request is received for a ContentItem with status "Published", the system shall set the status to "Draft", isPublished to false, and modifiedDate to the current timestamp.
If a publish request is received for a ContentItem with an empty or absent title, then the system shall refuse the request and show "Validation errors A value is required for Title".

The system shall maintain indexes on contentType, status, author, modifiedDate, and the composite (isLatest, isPublished) fields of the ContentItem entity.

stories.title: Create Tenant
stories.i_want: to create a new tenant with its recipe and database configuration
stories.so_that: the application can host an isolated site with its own content store
stories.description: Provision a new Tenant record with all required configuration. The tenant is created with status Uninitialized. The name must consist of letters only and be unique across all tenants. The databaseProvider defaults to Sqlite; a connection string is required for any non-Sqlite provider. recipeName must be one of the four supported values. Indexes are maintained on name and status for efficient lookup.
preconditions: The Administrator is authenticated
No tenant with the same name already exists

requirements.text: When a create-tenant request is received, the system shall persist a new Tenant record with the supplied id, name, description, requestUrlPrefix, recipeName, databaseProvider, databaseConnectionString, tablePrefix, databaseSchema, and featureProfile, setting status to 'Uninitialized'.
When a create-tenant request is received without a databaseProvider value, the system shall set databaseProvider to 'Sqlite'.
The system shall enforce uniqueness of the Tenant name field across all Tenant records.
The system shall maintain a database index on the Tenant name field.
The system shall maintain a database index on the Tenant status field.
If a create-tenant request omits the name field, then the system shall refuse the request.
If a create-tenant request omits the recipeName field, then the system shall refuse the request.
If the supplied recipeName is not one of 'Blog', 'Headless', 'Agency', or 'Blank', then the system shall refuse the request.
If the supplied databaseProvider is not one of 'Sqlite', 'SqlConnection', 'Postgres', or 'MySql', then the system shall refuse the request.
If the tenant name contains characters other than letters, then the system shall refuse the request.
If a Tenant record with the same name already exists, then the system shall refuse the request.
If the databaseProvider is not 'Sqlite' and no databaseConnectionString is supplied, then the system shall refuse the request.

stories.title: Enable Feature
stories.i_want: to enable a feature for the current tenant
stories.so_that: the feature's functionality becomes available in the site
stories.description: Enabling a feature sets isEnabled to true and marks the feature as recently installed. When force=true, unsatisfied dependencies are enabled automatically. When force=false (default), unmet dependencies cause the request to be refused. The External Authentication feature is auto-enabled when a dependent feature requires it, and its enabledByDependencyOnly flag is set. Features with isAlwaysEnabled=true are permanently treated as enabled.
preconditions: The Administrator is authenticated
The Feature catalogue has been seeded

requirements.text: When an enable-feature request is received for a disabled feature, the system shall set isEnabled to true for that Feature record.
When an enable-feature request successfully enables a feature, the system shall set isRecentlyInstalled to true for that Feature record.
When an enable-feature request is received with force set to true and the feature has unsatisfied dependencies, the system shall enable all dependency features before enabling the requested feature.

When enabling a feature causes the External Authentication feature to be activated as a dependency, the system shall set isEnabled to true and enabledByDependencyOnly to true for the External Authentication Feature record.
If an enable-feature request is received with force set to false and the feature has unsatisfied dependencies, then the system shall refuse the request.
If an enable-feature request specifies a featureId that does not exist in the catalogue, then the system shall return a not-found response.
While a Feature record has isAlwaysEnabled set to true, the system shall treat that feature as enabled regardless of the isEnabled flag value.

requirements.text: When a disable-feature request is received for an enabled feature with no enabled dependents, the system shall set isEnabled to false for that Feature record.
