If a disable-feature request is received with force set to false and other enabled features depend on the target feature, then the system shall refuse the request.
If a disable-feature request targets a Feature record with isAlwaysEnabled set to true, then the system shall refuse the request.
If a disable-feature request targets the External Authentication feature, then the system shall refuse the request.
If a disable-feature request specifies a featureId that does not exist in the catalogue, then the system shall return a not-found response.

stories.title: UserService Error Handling and Guard Conditions
stories.i_want: the UserService integration to handle failures safely and enforce the last-enabled-admin guard
stories.so_that: the system remains consistent and the last enabled administrator account is never removed
stories.description: The integration enforces null checks on user objects before any UserService call, invokes CancelAsync when an operation fails, records errors via UserService.reportError, and blocks any disable or delete operation that would remove the last enabled administrator.
preconditions: ASP.NET Core Identity is configured in the application.
At least one enabled administrator account exists.

requirements.text: The system shall perform a null check on the user object before invoking any UserService operation that requires a valid user.
When a UserService operation fails, the system shall invoke CancelAsync to roll back the in-progress operation.
When a UserService operation encounters an error, the system shall invoke UserService.reportError to record the error details.
If disabling or deleting a user would remove the last enabled administrator account, then the system shall refuse the operation and report the last-enabled-admin guard error.

integrations.behaviour: Enforces null checks before UserService calls; invokes CancelAsync on failure; records errors via UserService.reportError; blocks the last-enabled-admin guard on disable and delete operations.

business_rules: The last enabled administrator account cannot be disabled or deleted.

stories.title: Initiate External OAuth/OIDC Authentication
stories.i_want: to click an external SSO button on the login screen and be redirected to my chosen identity provider's consent screen
stories.so_that: I can authenticate using my existing Google, Microsoft, Facebook, Twitter, GitHub, or OpenID Connect account without creating a separate password
stories.description: When a user selects an external authentication provider on the login screen, the system initiates the OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorisation code flow by redirecting the browser to the provider's consent screen. The system validates that the provider is registered, checks whether new external registrations are permitted, and enforces rate limits configured by ExternalAuthenticationRateLimitsStartup.
preconditions: At least one external authentication provider is registered in the system configuration
The user is unauthenticated

requirements.text: When a user submits a valid provider name to the external authentication initiation endpoint, the system shall issue an HTTP 302 redirect to the corresponding external provider's consent screen.

If the submitted provider name is not registered in the system, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 400 with error code UNKNOWN_PROVIDER and message "Unknown external authentication provider."

If DisableNewExternalRegistrations is true and the requesting user has no existing account, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 403 with error code EXTERNAL_REGISTRATION_DISABLED and message "New external registrations are disabled."
The system shall enforce rate limits on calls to the external authentication initiation endpoint as configured by ExternalAuthenticationRateLimitsStartup.

stories.title: Complete External Authentication via Provider Callback
stories.i_want: the system to exchange the authorisation code returned by my identity provider and sign me in
stories.so_that: I receive an application authentication token and gain access without managing a separate password
stories.description: After the user consents at the external provider, the provider redirects back with an authorisation code and anti-CSRF state token. The system validates the state token, exchanges the code for an identity token, retrieves user profile claims, creates or matches the local user account, and returns an application authentication token with its expiry. When Redis is enabled, authentication tickets are stored in the distributed cache to support multi-instance deployments.
preconditions: The user has completed the external provider consent flow
The external provider has redirected back with an authorisation code and state token

requirements.text: When the callback endpoint receives a valid authorisation code, anti-CSRF state token, and provider name, the system shall exchange the code with the external provider, retrieve user profile claims, and return an application authentication token with its expiry.

If the external provider returns an error or the token exchange fails, then the system shall refuse authentication and return HTTP 401 with error code EXTERNAL_AUTH_FAILED and message "External authentication failed."

If DisableNewExternalRegistrations is true and the authenticating user has no existing local account, then the system shall refuse authentication and return HTTP 403 with error code EXTERNAL_REGISTRATION_DISABLED and message "New external registrations are disabled."
If the anti-CSRF state token in the callback does not match the expected value, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 401 with error code EXTERNAL_AUTH_FAILED.
While Redis is enabled for distributed caching, the system shall store authentication tickets in the distributed cache to support multi-instance deployments.

The Azure Communication Services email provider is configured with valid credentials under OrchardCore_Email_AzureCommunicationServices

When the system sends a verification email via Azure Communication Services, the system shall include the recipient email address, a subject line, and a verification link in the request body.

If Azure Communication Services returns an error response when sending a verification email, then the system shall log the delivery failure and notify the user that the verification email could not be delivered.

If the Azure Communication Services email provider is not configured when a user attempts to register, then the system shall refuse the registration and inform the user that email verification is unavailable.

stories.i_want: content items to be automatically indexed, re-indexed, and removed in Lucene when their lifecycle events occur
stories.so_that: the search index always reflects the current state of published content
stories.description: Whenever a content item is published, the system calls the OrchardCore.Lucene in-process library to add or update the document in the index. When a content item is updated and re-published the existing document is replaced. When a content item is removed or unpublished the corresponding document is deleted from the index. Only fields declared in the index mapping are submitted. Indexing errors are non-fatal and are written to the application log without interrupting the content operation.
preconditions: The Lucene search feature is enabled
At least one Lucene index is configured and the content item's type is mapped to that index

requirements.text: When a content item is published, the system shall submit the item's mapped fields to the Lucene index via the OrchardCore.Lucene in-process library.
When a published content item is updated and re-published, the system shall update the corresponding document in the Lucene index with the latest field values.
When a content item is removed, the system shall delete the corresponding document from the Lucene index.
When a content item is unpublished, the system shall remove the corresponding document from the Lucene index.
The system shall transmit only the content item fields declared in the Lucene index mapping to the Lucene index.
If the Lucene in-process library returns an error during a content lifecycle event, then the system shall log the error and allow the content operation to complete without interruption.

On execution the system passes the query parameters to the OrchardCore.Lucene in-process query engine and returns matching documents. Results support paging via from/size parameters. preconditions: The Lucene search feature is enabled

requirements.text: When an administrator creates a Lucene query, the system shall store the query name, target index name, and JSON query parameters.
When a Lucene query is executed, the system shall pass the stored JSON query parameters to the Lucene query engine via the OrchardCore.Lucene in-process library and return the matching documents.
The system shall support paging of Lucene query results using the from and size parameters supplied in the query JSON.
When an administrator updates a Lucene query, the system shall replace the stored query name, target index, and JSON query parameters with the new values.
When an administrator deletes a Lucene query, the system shall remove the query definition from the store.
If the Lucene query engine returns an error during query execution, then the system shall log the error and return an empty result set to the caller.
If a Lucene query references an index that does not exist, then the system shall log the error and return an empty result set to the caller.

stories.title: Authenticate and Authorize REST API Access
stories.i_want: to authenticate with the Content REST API using an API key or Bearer token
stories.so_that: my application can securely access content operations with the correct permissions
stories.description: The Content REST API accepts API key or Bearer token credentials and enforces the AccessContentApi permission as the authorization gate for all operations. Unauthenticated or unauthorized requests are rejected before any content operation is attempted.
preconditions: The Content REST API is deployed and reachable
The integration developer has been issued a valid API key or Bearer token

requirements.text: The system shall accept either a valid API key or a valid Bearer token as credentials for all requests to the Content REST API.
The system shall enforce the AccessContentApi permission as the authorization gate for all Content REST API endpoints.
If a request to the Content REST API arrives without a valid API key or Bearer token, then the system shall return HTTP 401 Unauthorized and reject the request.
If the authenticated caller does not hold the AccessContentApi permission, then the system shall return HTTP 403 Forbidden and reject the request.

If the content item JSON document in a POST /api/content request fails validation, then the system shall return HTTP 400 and include the validation error details in the response body.

When an authenticated caller posts a content item with a VersionOptions value of Published, Draft, or DraftRequired, the system shall invoke CreateAsync with the specified VersionOptions to produce the corresponding content version.

When an authenticated caller requests GET /api/content/{id} with a VersionOptions parameter of Published, Draft, or DraftRequired, the system shall return the content item version matching the specified VersionOptions.

stories.title: Execute a GraphQL Query to Retrieve Content Data
stories.i_want: to submit a GraphQL query to the API endpoint with a Bearer token
stories.so_that: I can retrieve content item data for headless and integrated applications
stories.description: An Integration Developer sends a POST request to /api/graphql with a GraphQL query string and optional variables. The system authenticates via Bearer token, checks the ExecuteGraphQL permission, executes the query, and returns the result as a JSON payload with a 'data' property. Unauthenticated or unauthorised requests, and syntactically invalid queries, receive a structured error response.
preconditions: The GraphQL API endpoint is available at POST /api/graphql
The Integration Developer holds a valid Bearer token
The authenticated account has the ExecuteGraphQL permission granted

requirements.text: When the system receives a POST /api/graphql request with a valid Bearer token and the ExecuteGraphQL permission, the system shall execute the supplied GraphQL query and return a JSON response containing a 'data' property.

When the system receives a POST /api/graphql request that includes a 'variables' property alongside the query string, the system shall bind those variables to the query before execution and include the resolved values in the response.

stories.description: Applies the YesSql session lifecycle pattern to every write operation across all entity types. Covers users, roles, content items, tenants, features, queries, and deployment plans.

The system shall call ISession.SaveAsync() in the finally block of every write operation handler.
If an exception occurs during a write operation, then the system shall call ISession.CancelAsync() to mark the session as invalid before the finally block executes.
The system shall apply the ISession lifecycle pattern to write operations for all entities: users, roles, content items, tenants, features, queries, and deployment plans.

stories.description: Implement local authentication using ASP.NET Core Identity (OrchardCore.Users). A user submits a username and password to POST /v1/auth/login; the system validates credentials against the identity store, returns a session token on success, and returns HTTP 401 for unknown username, wrong password, or disabled account. If the submitted password does not match the stored credential for the account, then the system shall refuse the login request and return HTTP 401.
If the target user account is disabled, then the system shall refuse the login request and return HTTP 401.
The system shall store all user passwords as a cryptographically secure one-way hash and never in plain text.

The system shall evaluate implied permissions so that granting a parent permission automatically grants all declared dependent permissions.
When an administrator saves role permissions, the system shall replace the complete permission set for that role with the submitted set.

preconditions: The RBAC framework (US-37a-04) is operational
The calling user holds the Administrator role

requirements.text: When an administrator submits a create-role request with a unique name, the system shall persist the new role and return HTTP 201.

When an administrator clones an existing role, the system shall create a new role containing all permissions of the source role.
When an administrator updates role permissions, the system shall replace all existing permissions for that role with the submitted permission set.
When an administrator deletes a custom role, the system shall remove the role and all its associated permissions.
If an administrator requests deletion of a system role, then the system shall refuse the request and return HTTP 403.
If the role referenced in a retrieve, update-permissions, or delete request does not exist, then the system shall return HTTP 404.

Index management applies uniformly to both Lucene and Elasticsearch providers.

At least one search provider feature is enabled (OrchardCore.Lucene or OrchardCore.Elasticsearch)

requirements.text: The system shall allow administrators to create named search indices specifying the index name, the content types to include, and the culture for both Lucene and Elasticsearch providers.
When an administrator triggers a rebuild on a search index, the system shall re-index all published content items whose content types are configured for that index.
When an administrator triggers a reset on a search index, the system shall remove all documents from the index and re-index all published content items of the configured content types.
When an administrator deletes a search index, the system shall remove the index definition and all of its indexed documents.
If an Elasticsearch indexing operation fails, then the system shall log the error and allow search to continue returning results from the last successful index state.

stories.title: Login Timing-Attack Normalization
stories.i_want: the login endpoint to perform a dummy hash verification whenever a submitted username is not found
stories.so_that: response times are uniform regardless of username validity and timing-based username enumeration is prevented
stories.description: When a login attempt is made for a non-existent username, the authentication service must execute a dummy bcrypt-equivalent hash verification before returning the invalid-credentials error. This normalises the response time to match the time taken for a valid username with a wrong password, eliminating the timing side-channel that would otherwise reveal whether a username is registered in the system.

The system shall ensure the response time for a login attempt with a non-existent username is statistically indistinguishable from the response time for a login attempt with an existing username and an incorrect password.
If username enumeration is attempted by comparing login response times, then the system shall return response times that do not allow an attacker to distinguish a valid username from an invalid one.
